$description: The design-token source for the mjx-ooxml-rs client platform (MJXOFF-156, re-seeded from hermes-universal by MJXOFF-271). It is TWO TIERS. The first is literal and is what a host overrides: the `color` palette, and — inside `theme` — the ~14 skin SEEDS and the ~11 mix KNOBS, whose CSS custom properties are byte for byte the ones `apps/hermes-universal/src/themes/context.tsx` writes inline on `:root` (`--theme-foreground`, `--theme-midground`, `--theme-background-seed`, `--theme-mix-chrome`, …). The second tier is DERIVED: a colour written as `{ "mix": [ … ] }` is a CSS `color-mix(in srgb, …)` of the first tier, and the surfaces, the text colours and the strokes are all derived rather than stated — which is what makes dark mode the same seeds with different knobs instead of a second palette, and what lets one overridden seed re-theme everything mixed from it. There is exactly ONE implementation of that mix, `mjx_tokens::color_mix`; the generator evaluates every derivation through it so all four artefacts carry the RESOLVED colour (a canvas needs a colour, not an expression), and `ui/tokens/derivations.css` restates the expressions for the browser so the cascade re-derives them. `ui/tokens/chromium-agreement.mjs` asserts that our one implementation and Chromium's agree, for every derived token, in both schemes. The `font`, `font-weight`, `text`, `leading`, `tracking`, `radius`, `spacing`, `shadow`, `ease` and `duration` groups are the allr.work values as measured in docs/client-platform/DESIGN_TOKENS.md §1. This file is the ONLY hand-edited artefact in the pipeline; ui/tokens/tokens.css, ui/tokens/derivations.css, ui/tokens/tokens.ts and crates/mjx-tokens/src/generated.rs are emitted from it by `cargo run -p xtask -- tokens`. FORMAT: W3C Design Tokens Community Group format, in its string profile — `color` is `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`, `dimension` is a CSS length such as `8px`, `duration` is `150ms`, `percentage` is `92%`. EXTENSIONS live under the `mjx` key: `rustType` names the struct a group becomes in Rust; `schemes` marks a group whose children are colour schemes; `usage` and `background` are the contrast metadata, required on every colour token.

color.$description: The Allr brand constants. Warm and organic: the neutrals are beige rather than grey and the `black` is a green. These are the raw ramp steps — `theme` names which of them plays which role, and derives the surfaces from them. The values are hermes-universal's own (`apps/hermes-universal/src/themes/presets.ts`, the `allr` skin), which is the same brand as DESIGN_TOKENS.md §1 measured from the site; where the two differ the product's value wins, because the point of the re-seed is that the editor and the app it is embedded in never disagree about a colour.

paper.$description: page background — warm off-white. DESIGN_TOKENS.md §1 measured `#fdfcf9` from the marketing site's stylesheet; hermes's `ALLR_PAPER` is this, and it is the value the surrounding application actually paints.

body.$description: the site's actual page background — warmer than `paper`, and hermes's sidebar seed (`ALLR_BODY`).

card.$description: raised surfaces. hermes's rule: `card` is the sole `#ffffff`, and it is a surface, never a text colour.

white.$description: true white; the site declares it beside `card` and this file keeps both names.

paper-neutral.$description: the warm neutral the chrome and sidebar seeds are mixed toward (`--theme-neutral-chrome` / `--theme-neutral-sidebar`). Without it a skin whose background seed is a strong colour would paint the whole chrome in it.

card-neutral.$description: the neutral the card and elevated seeds are mixed toward (`--theme-neutral-card`).

ink.$description: primary text — a deep, desaturated green-black (hermes's `ALLR_INK`, "deep pine"). It is also the dark scheme's card surface, which is what makes the dark theme read as the light theme's ink rather than as a grey product.

green.$description: primary accent. DESIGN_TOKENS.md §2.2: 3.39 : 1 on white — legal for UI components and large text, ILLEGAL for body text. Fills, borders, indicators and icons only; `green-deep` is the accent-coloured text colour.

green-deep.$description: accent, pressed / on-light text. DESIGN_TOKENS.md §2.2: 5.34 : 1 on white — legal for body text. hermes uses it as the CTA colour for exactly that reason.

green-lifted.$description: the dark scheme's accent-coloured text. hermes: "lifted off #2e9e63 — the brand green is tuned for white and drops below 4.5 : 1 against pine".

honey-deep.$description: secondary accent, deep. Measured at 3.49 : 1 on white by this generator, so — unlike `green-deep`, its counterpart in the green ramp — it is NOT legal for body text and is tagged `fill-only`. hermes reaches the same conclusion from the other direction: `#e9a83e` is 1.95 : 1 on paper and therefore invisible as a 1px focus ring, so honey-deep is the light scheme's `midground`.

clay.$description: hermes's `ALLR_CLAY` — the destructive colour, warm rather than a generic red.

font.$description: The site's three families. Young Serif is display-only — empty states and onboarding, never the chrome and never document content.

sans.$description: the chrome face; a rounded humanist that reads slightly wider than a typical UI font.

mono.$description: DESIGN_TOKENS.md §1 elides this stack after `Liberation Mono`; the elision is the standard Tailwind v4 monospace stack, written out here in full.

font-weight.$description: The four weights the site loads. DESIGN_TOKENS.md §1 records the values but not the custom-property names; these are Tailwind v4's own (`--font-weight-*`), which is the layer the site's theme is written in.

text.$description: The two small type sizes the site declares. Dense editor surfaces — the formula bar, the cell grid, a properties inspector — use `xs` with `leading.tight`, not the site's relaxed body measure.

body.$description: DESIGN_TOKENS.md §1 records this as `body line-height` with no custom-property name of its own; it joins the `leading` family here.

radius.$description: The radii are large, and that is the most recognisable part of the source's character. Toolbars and inspectors keep that softness rather than reverting to the 2–4px corners Office uses.

spacing.$description: The base spacing step, from which the site's spacing scale is multiplied. It is a token in its own right rather than a group so that its custom property is `--spacing`, exactly as the site declares it.

shadow.$description: Shadows are ink-tinted, never neutral black.

lift.$description: the site's one elevation, tinted with `color.ink` at 11% alpha.

ease.$description: `spring` overshoots: right for a panel or sheet entering, wrong for anything attached to a document object, where overshoot reads as imprecision. Selection, handles and canvas motion use `ink`.

duration.$description: DESIGN_TOKENS.md §1 records the site's `default duration` of 0.15s with no custom-property name of its own; it is named `--duration-transition` here for what it is.

theme.$description: The application theme, in both colour schemes and in three layers. SEEDS come first — the skin's raw colours, whose scheme-relative custom properties (`--theme-foreground`, `--theme-primary`, `--theme-midground`, `--theme-background-seed`, …) are exactly the names hermes-universal's `applyTheme()` writes inline on `:root`, so dropping this platform into that application re-themes it with no code. KNOBS come second — the mix percentages `applyTheme()` writes beside them. The SEMANTIC layer comes last and is mostly DERIVED from the two above by `color-mix(in srgb, …)`: that is why the dark scheme is not a second palette but the same expressions over different seeds, and why one overridden seed moves every surface, text colour and stroke that is mixed from it. The two schemes must carry exactly the same member names AND derive each of them the same way; the generator fails if either drifts.

foreground.$description: SEED. The ink every text colour and every stroke is mixed from. `--theme-foreground`.

primary.$description: SEED. The CTA colour — hermes uses green-deep rather than the brand green so small white label text on a primary control stays legible. `--theme-primary`.

midground.$description: SEED. What hermes calls the ring colour: focus rings, the streaming cursor, active pills, and — through the stroke knobs below — every border in the chrome. Honey-DEEP in the light scheme, because `#e9a83e` measures 1.95 : 1 on paper and a 1px ring in it is invisible. `--theme-midground`.

background-seed.$description: SEED. The chrome's own colour, before it is mixed toward `neutral-chrome`. `--theme-background-seed`.

neutral-chrome.$description: SEED. What the chrome seed is mixed toward, so that a strongly coloured skin still yields a habitable chrome. `--theme-neutral-chrome`.

mix-chrome.$description: KNOB. How much of `background-seed` survives into the chrome. `--theme-mix-chrome`.

mix-sidebar.$description: KNOB. `--theme-mix-sidebar`. Declared although no member below reads it yet: hermes writes all five surface knobs together, and a host that set four of five would otherwise leave the fifth silently at our default.

mix-bubble.$description: KNOB. `--theme-mix-bubble`. Declared for the reason `mix-sidebar` gives.

fill-primary-accent-mix.$description: KNOB. How much accent a primary fill carries. `--theme-fill-primary-accent-mix`.

text-primary.$description: The ink itself, and NOT hermes's `--ui-text-primary` (which is the ink at 94% alpha). ⚠ Measured, not preferred: this token must be opaque, because the contrast gate refuses a translucent text colour on the ground that it would be measured against a surface it is never seen on — and an opaque approximation of `rgba(ink, 0.94)` is only exact on the one surface it was composited over, which is a promise a primary text colour cannot keep across a background, a surface and a raised surface. Softening it also costs the palette its dynamic range: with primary text at 94% the picker's swatch indicator — which chooses between this and `surface` — bottomed out at 2.99 : 1 over the 4,352-colour sweep, below WCAG 1.4.11's floor. hermes's softening survives where it is a genuine hierarchy step rather than a texture, which is `text-secondary` at 74%.

text-secondary.$description: DERIVED — hermes's `--ui-text-secondary`, composited for the reason `text-primary` gives.

border.$description: DERIVED — hermes's `--ui-stroke-secondary`: a little accent over ink at low alpha, so strokes stay pine-and-lamplight rather than going grey against a warm surface. hermes mixes toward `transparent`; this mixes toward the background instead, which is the same colour once composited and is what keeps the token opaque and measurable.

accent.$description: Fills, borders, indicators and icons. NOT text — see `accent-pressed`.

accent-pressed.$description: The pressed accent, and the only accent-coloured text colour on a light surface.

accent-surface.$description: DERIVED — hermes's `--ui-bg-primary` shape, with two corrections that are measurements rather than taste. It tints the **surface** and not the chrome background, because an accent surface is a tinted surface and that is what it sits on. And it uses the SECONDARY fill knob: at the primary knob's 16% the accent surface reaches 4.23 : 1 against `accent-pressed`, and this pairing is a labelled button in the shared harness — below the 4.5 : 1 body-text minimum, on every story. The TERTIARY knob is the strongest tint at which the accent-coloured label stays legal in BOTH schemes: 4.76 : 1 light and 4.63 : 1 dark, against 4.23 and 3.90 at the primary knob. The dark side is the binding one, because there the accent fill and `accent-pressed` are near neighbours in lightness.

accent-border.$description: DERIVED — hermes's `--ui-stroke-primary` shape, in the accent rather than the ring colour, over the surface it is drawn on.

secondary-accent.$description: The ring colour, exposed under the name the chrome uses for it.

secondary-surface.$description: DERIVED. The secondary accent's own fill, mixed by the same knob and over the same surface as `accent-surface`, so the two ramps cannot drift apart — and so the contrast decision taken for one holds for the other.

foreground.$description: SEED. hermes's `allr` dark foreground — warm parchment, not white.

primary.$description: SEED. Lifted off the brand green so it clears 4.5 : 1 against pine.

midground.$description: SEED. Honey rather than honey-deep in the dark scheme: on pine it is the bright end of the ramp that reads, which is the mirror of the light scheme's reasoning rather than a different decision.

card-seed.$description: SEED. The dark card is the light scheme's ink — §2.1's whole claim, as a value.

elevated-seed.$description: SEED. hermes's `allr` dark popover is the same pine as its card; this lifts it to the skin's `muted` step instead, so a menu or a dialog is still told apart from the surface under it. That is a deliberate departure and the only one in this scheme.

neutral-chrome.$description: SEED. Warm pine neutrals rather than near-black — the dark skin is the light skin's ink, not a separate grey product.

fill-primary-accent-mix.$description: The accent-mix knobs are the same in both schemes — hermes's `:root.dark` overrides only the five surface knobs. They are restated rather than inherited so that the two schemes are the same shape, which is what lets the generator prove they are.

fill-tertiary-accent-mix.$description: ⚠ The one accent-mix knob this scheme overrides, and the reason is a measurement. It is the knob `accent-surface` and `secondary-surface` are tinted by, and the two schemes need opposite strengths: in the light scheme the accent-coloured label on that tint is DARK, so a strong tint is free, while here the label is LIGHT and every point of tint moves the fill toward it. At the light scheme's 8% the harness's preset button measures 4.36 : 1, under the 4.5 : 1 minimum; at 5% it is 4.68 : 1. hermes's `:root.dark` overrides four of the five surface knobs for the same kind of reason — a knob is per-scheme precisely so that one expression can serve both.

text-primary.$description: The parchment itself, for the reason the light scheme's counterpart gives at length.

accent.$description:
The brand green, in both schemes — kept `fill-only` for symmetry with the light scheme, where the same role fails body-text contrast. A component that may not colour text with the accent in one scheme may not do it in the other either.

⚠ It was `#4fc98a`, and that was a measured defect rather than a preference. In the light scheme the accent-coloured TEXT (`accent-pressed`, green-deep) is *darker* than the accent FILL, so a tint of the fill carries the text easily. `#4fc98a` inverted that relationship in the dark scheme — the fill was as light as `accent-pressed` — and no tint of it could carry an accent-coloured label: the harness's own preset button measured 3.90 : 1 at the primary fill knob and 4.17 : 1 at the tertiary one, both under the 4.5 : 1 minimum. The old hand-written dark palette had the same defect at 4.11 : 1 and it went unseen because the catalogue's a11y sweep runs the light story. The brand green is dimmer than `color.green-lifted`, which restores the light scheme's ordering and takes the pairing to 4.85 : 1, while still clearing the 3 : 1 non-text floor against the dark surface at 3.48 : 1.

accent-pressed.$description: The accent-coloured text colour on a dark surface.

document.$description: The document-surface palette. DESIGN_TOKENS.md §2.3: an editor has TWO palettes and conflating them is the classic mistake. The page stays true white in both schemes — a document is white paper, and a warm-tinted or dark page changes what the author sees relative to what they will print or send. What changes with the scheme is the canvas backdrop behind the page, the page shadow, and the in-canvas UI. A reading-mode inversion of the page itself is a user setting, not a theme consequence. These are the tokens the Rust canvas needs and a CSS custom property cannot reach it, which is the reason this pipeline emits four artefacts instead of one.

selection-alpha.$description: KNOB. How much of the accent a selection fill carries. It is a knob rather than a number inside the derivation because the two schemes want different strengths, and one `color-mix()` declaration has to serve both.

backdrop.$description: The chrome's own background behind a true-white page, which makes the page read as a distinct, lit object rather than dissolving into it.

page-border.$description: The page's edge is the chrome's own border colour, so the one place chrome meets canvas cannot disagree with itself.

selection-fill.$description: DERIVED. `color-mix(in srgb, C p%, transparent)` is an ALPHA operation and not a blend toward black — it yields the accent's own channels at `p%` alpha — which is why a selection fill can be written this way at all.

tracked-change-insert.$description: Tagged `fill-only`: measured against the page it does not reach 4.5 : 1, so it is legal for the change bar, the underline rule and the marker, and a tracked insertion's own glyphs must stay `theme.*.text-primary`.

tracked-change-delete.$description: Tagged `fill-only` for the same reason as `tracked-change-insert`.

selection-alpha.$description: KNOB. A little stronger than the light scheme's, because the same alpha over a dark backdrop reads weaker.

page.$description: True white in the dark scheme too — §2.3's whole point.

tracked-change-insert.$description: The page stays white in the dark scheme, so this is measured against white like its light-scheme counterpart.
